links.outcome: Accuracy of citations generated by chatbots verified against Scopus and Google Scholar
links.effect: Of 360 requested references, 273 generated; 128 of 190 validly formatted articles exactly matched real evidence, overall strict yield 35.6% (128/360). Grok 78.9% exact matches; Meta AI 0%.
links.quote: Fact-checking revealed that 128 of these 190 validly formatted articles (metadata accuracy rate: 67.4%) showed an exact match with real evidence, resulting in an overall strict yield of 35.6% (128/360) from the initial requested references.

links.outcome: Fabricated or incorrect references in AI outputs requiring verification before use
links.effect: Overall strict yield of real, exact-match references was 35.6% (128/360); Perplexity showed critical rates of total hallucination; Meta AI 0/10 exact matches.
links.quote: The results highlight the urgency of introducing structured AI literacy programs across medical education, promoting the use of such technologies exclusively as a complementary tool and always subject to rigorous human fact-checking.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking study evaluating the factual accuracy and hallucination rates of four generative AI chatbots (ChatGPT, Grok, Meta AI, Perplexity) in retrieving medical literature references.
